A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same YADL table-augmentation study. The full texts, including v5's Appendices A–C, support comparison across relocations. Although v5's Table 1 is clipped below page 7, its embedded text is recoverable and matches v3's Table 3.

before.justification: V3 Section 5 reports original prediction, runtime and memory experiments using YADL variants and Open Data US.

after.justification: V5 Section 5 and Appendix C report original benchmark results, including neural learner comparisons, ablations and computational measurements.

M1.justification: YADL construction, Hybrid MinHash and the join selectors remain substantively unchanged. First aggregation becomes Any: v3 retains the first duplicate, while v5 describes random or order-independent selection, yet Appendix C.7 still refers to first. The PDFs do not resolve whether this represents a procedural change or clarification of arbitrary row selection.

E1.justification: All five data lakes remain. V5's results for six base tables omit movie prediction and 2017–2022 US Accidents, which v3 includes in its experimental coverage. Movies nevertheless remains in v5 Appendix Table 9, leaving its participation in retained aggregate results unclear. The documented coverage contracts within the existing benchmark.

E2.justification: V5 adds ResNet and RealMLP to actual predictor comparisons alongside CatBoost and the linear baseline, now identified as RidgeCV (Table 3 and Figures 2 and 11). V3 compares only linear learning and CatBoost. The four retrieval comparators remain unchanged; Appendix C.1's other systems are discussed as unsuccessful integrations.

E3.justification: V3 compares methods against per-step averages; v5 documents fold-matched ablations against a fixed Exact Matching/Best Single Join/Any/CatBoost configuration. The containment–prediction analysis also changes from Stepwise Greedy in v3 Figure 8b to Best Single Join in v5 Figure 3. New neural evaluations use pytabkit defaults and GPUs. These are substantive changes in evaluation controls and settings.

E4.justification: V5 adds joint-configuration Pareto analyses of prediction versus runtime and memory, overall configuration rankings, and fixed-reference component ablations (Figures 2, 6, 9–14 and Table 3). Existing containment, top-1 retrieval and timing analyses are retained or revised. V3's separate lake-wise gain-over-unjoined-tables analysis in Figure 7 is no longer presented.

E5.justification: V5 introduces trimmed means with cutoff 0.2 and ± summaries in Table 8, plus critical-difference displays. It omits v3's explicit statement of ten outer cross-validation splits. The meaning of ± and the statistical procedure underlying the critical-difference plots are unspecified; additional runs or formal significance testing cannot be established.

E6.justification: V5 adds task-by-lake score tables and neural predictor results. For example, Table 3 reports RealMLP at −21.24% prediction difference and 32.79x runtime relative to the reference. Top-1 retrieval and amortized retrieval-time results also change. Revised coverage and controls prevent interpreting these as matched performance changes from v3. The RAM table and selector timing breakdown are retained.

T1.justification: The joinability and Jaccard-containment definitions remain equivalent. V5 makes the previously described Starmie scoring rule explicit, but introduces no substantive new theory, formal assumptions, proofs or derivations.

C1.justification: V3 prominently claims retrieval is the most consequential pipeline step, outweighing learner choice. V5 instead identifies the largest differences at the prediction stage and makes tree-based learners' effectiveness and resilience central findings in the abstract, results and conclusion. The YADL benchmark and pipeline contributions remain.

C2.justification: V5 adds explanations connecting missing values and high-cardinality categorical features to learner failures. It revises DFS from predominantly marginal benefit to useful but costly augmentation, and interprets Open Data US as competitive in some settings rather than generally weakest. Section 6 also adds a limitation claim about automated retrieval failing to replace human expertise.

D1.justification: Core YADL parameters, CatBoost settings and principal code/data access information are retained. V5 adds RidgeCV identification, pytabkit defaults, SLURM CPU/GPU execution details and compute accounting, plus modified baseline and wrapper access information in Appendix C. These extend documentation within the existing implementation framework.

R1.justification: V5 substantially repositions the study around AutoML and relational/tabular deep learning. New discussion and citations include RelBench, 4DBInfer, ResNet, RealMLP and missing-value research. Its explicit distinction between unknown-schema data lakes and schema-aware relational learning extends v3's predominantly database-oriented positioning.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, experimental narrative and conclusion are extensively rewritten. Detailed YADL construction and method descriptions move into Appendices A and B, while Appendix C combines retained analyses with new material. The main narrative shifts toward learning, computational trade-offs and practical configuration choices.

P2.justification: V5 adopts a single-column layout, redraws the pipeline diagram, adds Pareto and ranking displays and new result tables, and relocates many original figures and tables. It also introduces a substantial layout defect: most rows of Table 1 extend below page 7, whereas the corresponding v3 Table 3 is fully visible.

improvement.justification: The neural comparisons, fixed-reference ablations and configuration-specific Pareto analyses improve support for practical pipeline choices and address v3's limited examination of the learning stage. These gains are partly offset by narrower reported task coverage, omitted outer-validation details, undefined ± summaries and inconsistent captions, plus severe clipping of Table 1. The resulting losses in reproducibility and readability limit the net improvement.
